long_biography.plain_text:
Kragh grew up in Monticello, Indiana, where childhood drawing lessons began a lasting interest in design. He attended Western Kentucky University on a diving scholarship, discovered architecture through a drafting course and completed an architectural-technology degree. A master's degree at Illinois Institute of Technology preceded his move to Southwest Florida, where he developed from intern to principal architect.

In 2009, Kragh founded MHK Architecture in Naples. The practice became known for coastal residential work while broadening into commercial, hospitality and civic projects and opening studios across Florida, the Carolinas and Colorado. Kragh has paired design leadership with community service, including professional-association roles, charitable design work and board service. His work emphasizes regional character, client collaboration and buildings shaped around how people live.
